findings.reason: an author or worker that follows §1 or the followup body edits `reckon/cli.py` and changes nothing; the pointer must be corrected to `reckon/crew_follow_commands.py`.
findings.text: the plan states "`crew_follow`'s docstring in `reckon/cli.py`", but `crew_follow` and the docstring §3 rewrites live in `reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:2226`; `reckon/cli.py` contains no `crew_follow` definition and only re-exports `follower_row_path` at `reckon/cli.py:407`. Census of the same defect: the same wrong file is given in the followup body at docs/plans/a-follower-row-is-worth-a-wake.html:152 ("§3 and §4 both edit the follower in `reckon/cli.py`"), and that sentence is doubly stale because §4 is a landed investigation that changes no repository source. Section §3's own write paths name the correct file, so the plan is internally inconsistent about where the follower lives

findings.reason: §5's done-when should name the follower's own path object as the measurement driver and require the delay accessor be added to the owner (`RowPolicy`/`PaneRowPath` in `reckon/crew/ticker.py`) rather than read out of a private, so the number the plan reports is the owner's answer and not a fork's.
findings.text: §5 ("replay the measured week through the policy") needed a quantity its owner does not expose — the longest hold delay before release — and the measurement instrument forked its own driver and read the private hold map to get it: `pane_path._policy._held.values()` at reports/reckon/follower-row/week-replay/replay_week.py:117 and again at :124, with the instrument's own hand-built `PaneRowPath(...)` at :278–280 instead of the owner's measurement entry point. The owner is `replay_row_policy` (`reckon/crew/ticker.py:1633`), whose docstring says explicitly that "the measurement is taken through `PaneRowPath` … rather than through the policy alone", and the follower-side owner is `follower_row_path` (`reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:775`); `replay_row_policy` is used by the instrument only as a count cross-check (:167–168, :405), not as the driver. This is the type §1 itself warns of, said of `_follow_gap_rows` and the re-announce path: a second reader of the same state. Census: the only repository-wide reach into a policy private is this one file (repo grep for `._policy` / `._held` finds none in `reckon/` or `tests/`), so the defect is confined to the §5 instrument — but it is the instrument this plan's headline "54% fewer rows, longest delay 300 s" number rests on

response_events.reason: §5 has landed; the replay script is a one-off measurement kept outside the repository, and its review recorded this same follow-on. Exposing a hold-delay reader from RowPolicy for one measurement would add public surface that nothing else would use.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan adds no module; the remaining work routes through the existing `PaneRowPath`, which already hides selection, hold policy and pane memory behind one object at `reckon/crew/ticker.py:1530`.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the §5 week-replay measured the hold delay by reaching into `PaneRowPath._policy._held`, a private the owner does not expose, instead of extending the owner or driving through `replay_row_policy`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1623, cli_options 351, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23, all unchanged by this plan; §3 adds no CLI option, no public definition, mcp view or refusal family, and says in its own text why (the producer's log already prints every row), which is the required accounting for added surface even when the surface added is none.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan searched the codebase and cites the mechanisms it extends, but its account of prior art names the wrong file for `crew_follow`'s docstring.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the plan adds no wrapper; §3 changes a decision inside `RowPolicy` and rewrote a docstring, and explicitly declines to add a `crew follow` option rather than layering one.
